note: Plan-only prompts on a fresh claude-opus-5-5 subagent; control without the skill. Grade from the answer text. The skill adds the background-wait and check-state rules; the self-matching pgrep loop is lived evidence from a real session, not reproduced here. evals.prompt: I just pushed branch feat/x and started `bun run build` in the background in another shell. Wait until the CI run for the push finishes and until that build process ends, then tell me the results. Give the exact shell commands you would run; do not run them.
evals.expected_output: gh run watch <id> --exit-status or gh pr checks --watch; process wait by PID (kill -0) or a bracketed pgrep pattern; no `while pgrep -f "bun run build"` that matches its own shell; every loop bounded
assertions: the CI run is matched to the pushed commit SHA (e.g. `--commit`), not `--limit 1` on the branch
every watch command and PID loop has an explicit deadline
evals.with_skill_result: 2026-10-11 claude-opus-5-5 with the skill: pass on all assertions. pgrep-wait: run found by `--commit` and workflow with a bounded wait, `timeout 60m gh run watch`, PID from `pgrep -f '[b]un run build'` waited with `timeout 30m` around a kill -0 loop, both in the background with logs. registry-poll: kept `last`, exited 1 on timeout. Compared with the control, only registry-poll differs.
